description.value: A code that indicates the status of the concept. Typical values are active, experimental, deprecated, and retired

definition.value: A required binding, for use when the binding strength is 'extensible' or 'preferred'. This is deprecated - it is equivalent to `required`
The minimum allowable value set - any conformant system SHALL support all these codes
This value set is used as a required binding (in addition to the base binding (not a replacement), usually in a particular usage context)
This value set is used as an extensible binding (in addition to the base binding (not a replacement), usually in a particular usage context)

New records captured by the originating system SHALL only include this element if it contains a code from this value set. This binding imposes no expectations on legacy or externally sourced records. The definitions of 'legacy' or 'externally sourced' content are difficult, since systems often create new records based on pre-existing data and the boundaries around what is a distinct 'external' system can be fuzzy. The guide should define or reference guidance for how such definitions will be evaluated for the purpose of evaluating conformance.

New records captured by the originating system SHALL attempt to map the data they capture to this value set. If the mapping determines that it is possible to convey the concept at some level of granularity using a code from the value set, then that code shall be present in the instance. This binding imposes no expectations on legacy or externally sourced records. The definitions of 'legacy content' and 'externally sourced content' are difficult, since systems often create new records based on pre-existing data and the boundaries around what is a distinct 'external' system can be fuzzy. The guide should define or reference guidance for how such definitions will be evaluated for the purpose of evaluating conformance. This purpose should only be used for bindings where it's possible for a concept to NOT fall within the value set. If the value set includes broad all-encompassing codes or a code that conveys the concept of 'other', then use 'current' rather than 'current-extensible'.

Instances are strongly encouraged to have a code from this value set and, if they enable the "best practice" validation mode, they will receive a 'best practice violation' message for data elements that do not include a code from this value set.
A grouper for binding codes that do not impose formal conformance expectations, though some of them may result in information or best practice validation messages.
This value set is a candidate to substitute for the overall conformance value set in some situations; usually these are defined in the documentation
This is the value set that is preferred in a given context (documentation should explain why)
This value set is provided for user look up in a given context. Typically, these valuesets only include a subset of codes relevant for input in a context
This value set is a good set of codes to start with when designing your system
This value set is a component of the base value set. Usually this is called out so that documentation can be written about a portion of the value set
